extracted.intended_audience: NASA employees and public affairs officers (Headquarters, Centers, and component facilities)
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level policy and procedures governing what information may be released to news and information media, who may speak for NASA, coordination/concurrence requirements, and protections for classified or sensitive information. Applies to Headquarters, Centers, and component facilities and directs roles/responsibilities for public affairs activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of public information (Scope)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public information is defined as information in any form provided to news and information media, especially information that has the potential to generate significant media, or public interest or inquiry. Examples include, but are not limited to, press releases, media advisories, news features, and web postings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and explicit exclusions: Not included are scientific and technical reports, web postings designed for technical or scientific interchange, and technical information presented at professional meetings or in professional journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability (who the policy covers)
rubrics_metrics.description: This policy applies to NASA Headquarters, NASA Centers, and Component Facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is any conflict between this policy and any other NASA policy, directive, or regulation, this policy shall govern and supersede any previous issuance or directive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — commitment to openness
rubrics_metrics.description: NASA is committed to a culture of openness with the media and public that values the free exchange of ideas, data, and information as part of scientific and technical inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific and technical information from or about Agency programs and projects will be accurate and unfiltered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — prompt, factual, complete release
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of public information concerning NASA activities and the results of NASA activities will be made promptly, factually, and completely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with statutory responsibility to provide for the widest practicable and appropriate dissemination of information concerning its activities and the results thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — coordination to ensure timely release
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure timely release of information, NASA will endeavor to ensure cooperation and coordination among the Agency’s scientific, engineering, and public affairs communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — employees may speak about their work (with limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: NASA employees may, consistent with this policy, speak to the press and the public about their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such speaking must be consistent with other policy constraints in the directive (e.g., coordination requirements, restrictions on classified or SBU information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle — prohibition on disclosure of exempt/restricted information
rubrics_metrics.description: This policy does not authorize or require disclosure of information that is exempt from disclosure under FOIA or otherwise restricted by statute, regulation, Executive Order, or other Executive Branch policy or NASA policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of information not releasable include classified information, procurement sensitive information, Privacy Act information, other SBU information, and privileged pre-decisional information or attorney-client communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assistant Administrator for Public Affairs responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for developing and administering an integrated Agency-wide communications program, establishing Agency public affairs policies and priorities, and coordinating and reviewing performance of all Agency public affairs activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Will develop criteria to identify which news releases and other types of public information will be issued nationwide by NASA Headquarters; decisions to release nationwide will be made by the Assistant Administrator or designee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission Directorate Associate Administrators and Mission Support Office heads — accuracy responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Have ultimate responsibility for the technical, scientific, and programmatic accuracy of all information related to their respective programs and released by NASA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public affairs officers assigned to Mission Directorates — coordination and editing role
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Assistant Administrator’s direction, mission-assigned public affairs officers are responsible for timely and efficient coordination of public information covering their programs, including review by appropriate Mission Directorate officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes editing by public affairs staff to ensure products are well written and appropriate for audience, but editing shall not change scientific or technical data or the meaning of programmatic content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center Public Affairs Directors — implementation and quality control
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for implementing their portion of the Agency’s communications program, adhering to policies/procedures/priorities, coordinating with Headquarters as appropriate, and responsible for the quality of public information prepared by Center public affairs officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also responsible for day-to-day production of public information covering Center activities, obtaining necessary Center concurrences, and coordinating with Headquarters public affairs officers; must provide proper notification to NASA Office of Public Affairs prior to release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Center Directors — accuracy responsibility for local information
rubrics_metrics.description: Have ultimate responsibility for the accuracy of public information that does not require the concurrence of Headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Public information coordination and concurrence section for what requires Headquarters concurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to coordinate with public affairs before releasing media-generating information
rubrics_metrics.description: All NASA employees are required to coordinate, in a timely manner, with the appropriate public affairs officers prior to releasing information that has the potential to generate significant media or public interest or inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory coordination requirement; failure could trigger corrective action under other policy provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public affairs notification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All NASA public affairs officers are required to notify the appropriate Headquarters public affairs officers in a timely manner about activities or events that have the potential to generate significant media or public interest or inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public affairs code of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: All NASA public affairs employees are expected to adhere to the following code of conduct: Be honest and accurate; Honor publication embargoes; Respond promptly to media requests and respect deadlines; Act promptly to correct mistakes; Promote the free flow of scientific and technical information; Protect non-public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are explicit behavioral expectations for public affairs staff and inform adjudication of conduct or disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to coordinated release plans and schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: All NASA employees are responsible for adhering to plans (including schedules) for activities established by public affairs offices and senior management for the coordinated release of public information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public affairs plan requirement for NASA-funded missions
rubrics_metrics.description: All NASA-funded missions will have a public affairs plan, approved by the Assistant Administrator for Public Affairs, managed by Headquarters and/or a designated NASA Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public affairs activities for NASA-funded missions will not be managed by non-NASA institutions unless authorized by the Assistant Administrator for Public Affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption — Office of Inspector General activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of this directive do not apply to the Office of Inspector General regarding its activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination — general requirement for review and clearance
rubrics_metrics.description: All NASA employees involved in preparing and issuing public information are responsible for proper coordination among Headquarters, Center, and Mission Directorate offices to include review and clearance by appropriate officials prior to issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination procedures will be developed and published by the NASA Assistant Administrator for Public Affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination — mutual notification and keeping informed
rubrics_metrics.description: Headquarters and Center public affairs officers are required to coordinate to obtain review and clearance by appropriate officials, keep each other informed of changes, delays, or cancellations, and provide advance notification of the actual release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to ensure timely release and reduce conflicts/duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination — required reviews for scientific/programmatic accuracy and writing quality
rubrics_metrics.description: All public information shall be coordinated through appropriate Headquarters offices, including review by the Mission Directorate Associate Administrator and mission support office head (or designees) to ensure scientific, technical, and programmatic accuracy, and review by the Assistant Administrator of Public Affairs (or designee) to ensure products are well written and appropriate for the intended audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centers may issue institutional/local releases without full Headquarters coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: Centers may, without full coordination of Headquarters, issue public information that is institutional in nature, of local interest, or has been deemed not to be a Headquarters release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These releases must still be coordinated through appropriate Center offices and approved by the Center Director and Center Public Affairs Director; the Center Public Affairs Director must notify NASA Office of Public Affairs, Headquarters, prior to release. The Assistant Administrator will publish guidelines for what Centers may issue without Headquarters clearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dispute resolution process for release decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any dispute arising from a decision to proceed or not proceed with issuance of a news release or other public information will be addressed and resolved by the Assistant Administrator for Public Affairs with the appropriate Mission Directorate Associate Administrator, mission support office head, Center Director, and others as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Mission Directorate Associate Administrator shall be the arbiter of disputes about accuracy/characterization of programmatic, technical, or scientific information; additional appeals may be made to the Chief of Strategic Communications and to the Office of the Administrator. Written explanations of resolutions will be provided upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized spokespersons for Agency positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Only spokespersons designated by the Assistant Administrator for Public Affairs, or his/her designee, are authorized to speak for the Agency in an official capacity regarding NASA policy, programmatic, and budget issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits who may represent official Agency positions to designated individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer of knowledgeable spokespersons and journalist access to officials
rubrics_metrics.description: NASA will offer articulate and knowledgeable spokespersons who can best serve media/public needs; journalists may have access to the NASA officials they seek, provided those officials agree to be interviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balances centralized spokesperson selection with journalists' requests for access to specific officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee interviews — notification and coordination
rubrics_metrics.description: NASA employees may speak to the media about their work but shall notify their immediate supervisor and coordinate with their public affairs office in advance whenever possible (or immediately thereafter) and are encouraged to have a public affairs officer present during interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a public affairs officer is present, their role is to attest to content, support the interviewee, and provide post-interview follow up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency neutrality on scientific conclusions and personal views labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: NASA, as an Agency, does not take a position on any scientific conclusions; NASA scientists may draw conclusions and communicate them, but employees presenting personal views outside their official expertise must make clear they are presenting individual views and request to be sourced as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is guidance to distinguish Agency positions from individual scientific opinions in media interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on use of appropriated funds for media beyond official scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriated funds may only be used to support Agency missions and objectives consistent with legislative or presidential direction; government funds shall not be used for media interviews or communications that go beyond Agency responsibilities and/or an employee’s official area of expertise or responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-record default for media interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Media interviews will be “on-the-record” and attributable to the person making the remarks, unless authorized otherwise by the Assistant Administrator for Public Affairs or Center Public Affairs Director (or designees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any NASA employee providing material to the press will identify himself/herself as the source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio recordings during interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Audio recordings may be made by NASA with consent of the interviewee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employees not required to speak to the media
rubrics_metrics.description: NASA employees are not required to speak to the media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This clarifies that voluntary participation is allowed but not mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteered information not exclusive
rubrics_metrics.description: Public information volunteered by a NASA official will not be considered exclusive to any one media source and will be made available to other sources if requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on release of classified information
rubrics_metrics.description: Release of classified information in any form to the news media is prohibited; disclosure to unauthorized individuals may be cause for prosecution and/or disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignorance of policy does not excuse unauthorized release; internal guidance cited (NPR 1600.1) and Executive Order/implementing directives referenced for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting attempts to obtain classified information
rubrics_metrics.description: Any attempt by news media representatives to obtain classified information will be reported through Headquarters Office of Public Affairs or Installation Public Affairs Office to the Installation Security Office and Office of Security and Program Protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: DD Form 254 handling for classified operations
rubrics_metrics.description: For classified operations/programs managed under a DD Form 254, all inquiries concerning the activity will be responded to by the PAO official designated in Item 12 on the DD Form 254.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for classified information owned by other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: For classified operations/information owned by other Government agencies, all inquiries will be referred to the appropriate Agency public affairs officer as established in written agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBU information — accountability and approval required
rubrics_metrics.description: All NASA sensitive but unclassified (SBU) information requires accountability and approval for release; release to unauthorized personnel is prohibited and may result in prosecution/disciplinary action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignorance of policy does not excuse unauthorized release; internal guidance cited (NPR 1600.1) for identification, marking, accountability, and release procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of SBU information
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include proprietary information under nondisclosure agreements; source selection and bid/proposal information; information subject to export control (ITAR/EAR); Privacy Act information; predecisional materials; pending reorganizations or sensitive travel itineraries; information indicating government intentions/capabilities/operations that could threaten operations security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordination and concurrence before releasing SBU information
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon request for access to information/material deemed SBU, coordination must be made with the information/material owner to determine if it may be released; other organizations (General Counsel, External Relations, Procurement, etc.) must be consulted for assistance/concurrence prior to release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires multi-office consultation for SBU decisions and assigns accountability to the material owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of SBU requests from other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for SBU information from other Government agencies must be referred to the respective Agency public affairs officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia materials availability policy
rubrics_metrics.description: NASA’s multimedia material, from all sources, will be made available to the information media, the public, and all Agency Centers utilizing contemporary delivery methods and emerging digital technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centers must provide selected prints and original/duplicate files of news-oriented imagery and other digital multimedia, selected video in the highest quality format practical for news feed/features, audio/video files of significant news developments, and interactive multimedia features for incorporation into the Agency’s Internet portal.

rubrics_metrics.name: International activities — prior coordination and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases involving NASA activities, views, programs, or projects involving another country or an international organization require prior coordination and approval by the Headquarters offices of External Relations and Public Affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centers and Headquarters offices must report proposed visits by foreign news media representatives to the public affairs officer for the Office of External Relations for appropriate handling consistent with NASA policies and procedures.
